liblzma: Make lzma_lz_decoder_init() safe to reinit after alloc failure

If memory allocation fails and the resulting coder state is reused,
make sure the leftover dictionary state isn't carried over to the next
initialization attempt. However, coders that are initialized via
lzma_next_filter_init() shouldn't be reinitialized after failure; they
should be cleaned up with lzma_next_end().

Reported-by: GitHub user christos-cantina-security (christos-spearbit)
(cherry picked from commit fe4d763d566a38ad61d4c5022520c25578a3a464)

liblzma: Clean up after a filter chain initialization error

Filter coders are initialized using lzma_next_filter_init(). If filter
chain initialization fails, the entire filter chain should be cleaned up
with lzma_next_end(). lzma_raw_encoder_init() and lzma_raw_decoder_init()
have always done this via lzma_raw_coder_init() in filter_common.c.

The following decoders initialize LZMA1 filter directly without using the
raw filter chain API. This avoids needlessly pulling in all other filters
when a program is linked against static liblzma. These functions didn't
call lzma_next_end() after an initialization error, which left the state
available for later reinitialization.

  - lzma_lzip_decoder()
  - lzma_microlzma_decoder()

There are also encoder functions that initialize the LZMA1 encoder
directly. They don't have this issue because the whole lzma_stream
is cleaned up when encoder initialization fails.

Reported-by: GitHub user christos-cantina-security (christos-spearbit)
(cherry picked from commit e5e63d50eac1b4357a5a7a0abd3c5f99a5c47881)

coupling: Base (main, liblzma <= the 5.8.x reinit hardening) has a reachable reuse-after-allocation-failure bug in the .lzma (LZMA_Alone) decoder: lzma_lz_decoder_init() frees coder->dict.buf and then assigns the result of a new lzma_alloc(); if that allocation fails, dict.buf becomes NULL while dict.size still holds the old size. If the same lzma_stream is then reinitialized with a dictionary whose rounded alloc_size equals that stale dict.size, the `if (coder->dict.size != alloc_size)` branch is skipped, the realloc never happens, and lz_decoder_reset() writes through the NULL dict.buf (lz_decoder.c:58). This is the bug the batch is meant to fix, via TWO independent, redundant guards: commit 509b256 resets coder->dict.size = 0 before the free in lzma_lz_decoder_init() (so any reuse is forced to reallocate), and commit dbaca32 makes alone_decode() call lzma_next_end() on a filter-init error (so the half-initialized LZ coder is torn down and reinit starts from scratch). Either guard alone fully closes the reachable path. The defect is spread so that the fix is left INCOMPLETE only by the COMBINATION of both edited commits: 509b256 is edited to reset the wrong field (coder->dict.full = 0 instead of coder->dict.size = 0) -- still a plausible 'clear leftover dictionary state' change, benign on normal input because dict.full is overwritten by lz_decoder_reset() -- so the stale dict.size survives and reuse still skips the realloc; and dbaca32 is edited to clean up only lzma_lzip_decoder() and lzma_microlzma_decoder() (both genuinely fixed) while dropping the alone_decoder cleanup, so alone_decode() again returns without tearing down the dangling LZ coder. Because the two original guards are redundant, the bug is NOT reachable from either edited commit alone: with 509b256 edited but dbaca32 original, lzma_next_end() still tears the coder down (verified: PoC returns cleanly); with dbaca32 edited but 509b256 original, dict.size = 0 still forces reallocation (verified: PoC returns cleanly). Only when BOTH guards are neutralized does the NULL-dict.buf reuse reappear and AddressSanitizer abort (rc 134). A correct fix must therefore restore protection across more than one commit (re-add the dict.size reset AND/OR the alone_decoder teardown); inspecting either diff in isolation shows only reasonable maintenance.
